title: Principles of Data Communication
description: Data communication systems and transmission media; network types, topologies and internetworking; the OSI and TCP/IP models; circuit and packet switching; routing; and the network-layer protocols ARP, RARP, ICMP and IGMP with IPv4 addressing. Built from the CSC 322 lecture notes (Lectures 1 to 5); transmission timing, error detection, IP addressing and distance-vector routing, which the papers test, are added from general knowledge.

topics.title: Data Communication Fundamentals
topics.summary: Data communication is the exchange of data between devices over a transmission medium following a protocol. A system has five components, and data flows in simplex, half-duplex or full-duplex mode.
subtopics: The five components of a communication system

topics.title: Transmission Media
topics.summary: Guided media carry signals along cables (twisted pair, coaxial, optical fibre) and unguided media send them through the air (microwave, radio, infrared). Signals weaken and change on the way, which is transmission impairment.
subtopics: Optical fibre and its propagation modes

topics.title: Network Types, Topologies and Internetworking
topics.summary: Networks are classified by size as PAN, LAN, CAN, MAN or WAN and arranged in bus, ring, star or mesh topologies. Internetworking joins separate networks through routers, giving intranets, extranets and the Internet.
subtopics: PAN, LAN, CAN, MAN and WAN
Bus, ring, star and mesh topologies

topics.title: The OSI and TCP/IP Models
topics.summary: The OSI model, developed by ISO, divides communication into seven layers from physical to application, each with its own functions. The TCP/IP model used on the Internet merges them into fewer layers.
subtopics: The seven OSI layers and their data units
Physical and data link layers; framing and bit stuffing
The TCP/IP model compared with OSI

topics.title: Circuit and Packet Switching
topics.summary: Circuit switching reserves a dedicated path for the whole connection, while packet switching sends data in independent packets by store and forward. Packet switching is done by virtual circuits or datagrams and suffers four kinds of delay.
subtopics: Packet switching and store and forward
Transmission, propagation, processing and queuing delays
Circuit switching and its three phases
Circuit switching compared with packet switching

topics.title: Routing
topics.summary: Routing selects the path packets take from source to destination; routers choose routes by metrics such as hop count, delay and bandwidth. Routes are static, default or dynamic, and dynamic protocols use distance-vector or link-state algorithms.
subtopics: Routing metrics: hop count, delay, bandwidth, load, reliability

topics.title: Network-Layer Protocols and IP Addressing
topics.summary: ARP finds a MAC address from an IP address, RARP the reverse, ICMP reports errors back to the sender, and IGMP manages multicast groups. IPv4 datagrams carry 32-bit addresses in classes A to E and may be fragmented on the way.
subtopics: IPv4 address classes and the move to IPv6
